newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICA RESTORE PRIDE IN FINAL TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICA RESTORE PRIDE IN FINAL TEST.

text.p: South Africa salvaged some pride from their series defeat by the British Lions with a deserved 35-16 victory in the third and final test at Ellis Park on Saturday.

South Africa outscored the Lions in tries once again -- scoring four to the Lion's sole effort by scrum-half Matt Dawson -- but also had the boot of debutant fly-half Jannie de Beer to hammer over the kicks.
De Beer converted five out of his seven kicks at goal before going off with a head injury to ensure the Springboks were never headed as they again pounded away at the staunch Lions' defence.
The tourists were guilty of giving away too many penalties and could not recapture the focus which had helped them to victory in the first two tests.

They found themselves trailing to two de Beer penalties and a converted try from centre Percival Montgomery after just 16 minutes and although three Neil Jenkins penalties closed the gap to 13-9 at the interval, the Springboks' greater desire told in the second half.
